cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository, so the token
# can write to pull requests opened from forks (plain `pull_request` gets a
# read-only token there). This is only safe because the workflow never checks
# out or executes code from the pull request; PR metadata is handled as data
# and passed through environment variables, never interpolated into scripts.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Welcome and label
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Label and comment
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh label create needs-triage --color FBCA04 \
            --description "Awaiting maintainer triage" 2>/dev/null || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label needs-triage
          printf 'Welcome, @%s! Thanks for opening a pull request: **%s**\n\nA maintainer will triage it soon.\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$PR_TITLE" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage workflow

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened. It:

- posts a comment welcoming the author by username and repeating the pull request title;
- applies the `needs-triage` label (creating it if it does not exist).

It uses the `pull_request_target` trigger so the token can write to pull
requests opened from forks. For that reason the workflow never checks out or
runs code from the pull request, and the title and username are passed through
environment variables rather than interpolated into the script. Keep it that
way when editing it.
EOF

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and a "Triage workflow" section in `README.md`. I haven't run the workflow, because it needs a real pull request on GitHub.

When a pull request is opened, the workflow:
- **Label:** applies `needs-triage`, and creates the label first if the repo doesn't have it.
- **Comment:** posts `Welcome, @<username>! Thanks for opening a pull request: **<title>**`, followed by a line saying a maintainer will triage it soon.

**Fork handling:** it uses the `pull_request_target` trigger. A normal `pull_request` trigger gives forks a read-only token, so the comment and label would fail. With `pull_request_target`, the job runs with the base repo's token and can write to the pull request.

**Safety:**
- `pull_request_target` is only safe if the workflow never runs code from the pull request, so it never checks out the PR.
- The title and username go through environment variables, not straight into the script, so a crafted title can't inject commands.
- Permissions are limited to `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`.
- The README notes these constraints so later edits keep them.

A pull request title containing an `@name` will notify that person, because the title is repeated verbatim in the comment.
